persons.note: An Ottawa by birth who married into a Potawatomi band of the Illinois River and later led it; in 1812 an aide to Tecumseh. By his own account, as Matson took it down, he set out for Chicago when he heard the warriors had gone there, and came in a few hours after the fight on the 15th with twenty-two men; Andreas thinks he was not there before it. As Chamblee he signed the 1816 treaty that ceded the land about Chicago. He kept to peace in 1832, was granted land at Shabbona Grove and lost it, and died near Morris, Illinois, in July 1859.
